title: French colonial empire
summary: France’s overseas empire grew from Champlain’s founding of Quebec in 1608. At its peak New France stretched from the Gulf of St. Lawrence to Louisiana, until it was ceded to Britain in 1763. A second expansion began with the conquest of Algeria in 1830 and took in French West Africa, run as a federation from Senegal, and Indochina. After the Second World War nationalist movements grew: France left Indochina after Dien Bien Phu fell in 1954, French West Africa was independent by 1960, and Algeria in 1962.

uncertainty.note: Dated from Samuel de Champlain's founding of Quebec in 1608 to Algerian independence in 1962, marking the end of France's major overseas colonial empire.

as_recorded.value: He is also credited with founding Quebec City in 1608.
Algeria emerged from subsequent French rule in 1962.
